messages:
maria.chen: We received a DSAR referencing a file in legacy SFTP archive for redacted@example.com. Requester asks for erase + proof.
jamal: That archive objects are encrypted with `rw-legacy-key-v1`. We rotated wrappers last year; need to confirm decrypt path before any deletion.
eli: I checked KMS: primary key still available but IAM bindings were tightened. We should use a time-bound service account grant rather than loosening key policy.
security-bot: retention-exception candidate auto-created (#SE-9744). Reminder: any RBAC exceptions must be documented.
ops-tom: I can create an ephemeral grant to service-account:sftp-erasure@infra for decrypt only. Suggest 3 hours.
maria.chen: 3h ok. Legal, what evidence do you require to close DSAR?
legal-sara: Need a manifest showing which objects were deleted tied to the requester identifier, KMS audit logs for decrypt calls, and a short attestation about snapshot/backups handling. Prefer NDJSON manifest + log snippets.
jamal: Note: older tar snapshots (sftp-archive/snapshots/*.tar.gz) may still contain the file. Options: redact affected snapshots, rotate wrapper and attest inaccessibility, or targeted snapshot rewrite. Legal prefers targeted redact when possible.
eli: Ops plan: 1) request 3h grant; 2) run safe-delete: list -> verify -> delete; emit NDJSON proof entries like {"object":"sftp-archive/users/redacted@example.com/msg1.txt","action":"delete","by":"service-account:sftp-erasure@infra","ts":"2026-03-21T10:12:03Z"}; 3) collect KMS decrypt audit entries; 4) open retention-exception if snapshots need rewrite.
ops-tom: Grant command (internal): `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding rw-legacy-key-v1 --member=serviceAccount:sftp-erasure@infra --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition='request.time < "2026-03-21T13:30:00Z"'`
maria.chen: Important: do NOT grant broader roles. Keep scope minimal and timeboxed.
ops-tom: Dry-run output sample: {"object":"sftp-archive/users/redacted@example.com/msg1.txt","found_in":"snapshots/20210103.tar.gz","action":"dry-run"}
eli: After dry-run we'll run delete and then scan snapshots to identify redaction targets.
legal-sara: 2 years of KMS log retention is fine for DSAR evidence. We'll need signed attestation for any key-rotation-as-inaccessibility approach.
maria.chen: Assigning: ops-tom -> run delete & upload manifest; eli -> collect KMS logs & draft attestation if needed; me -> file retention-exception draft and coordinate with Legal. Keep this thread as single source of approvals.
ops-tom: Deletion completed at 2026-03-21T11:22Z. Pushed NDJSON manifest + KMS snippets to ticket SE-9744.
eli: Uploaded KMS decrypt audit lines and operation summary to ticket.
legal-sara: Drafted confirmation statement. Will sign once artifacts are verified.
security-bot: Reminder: revoke ephemeral grant at expiry.
maria.chen: Thanks team. No permanent key policy changes. We'll close DSAR after Legal signs.
